purpose: Synthetic document-reader regression examples for source ranges, retained context, and extraction limitations.

cases.name: Multiline formatting rule and a dependent paragraph
cases.source:
## Formatting

- **Write reports with [format.js](format.js).** Every report under
  `reports/` contains a `title` and an `items` array. The report
  includes a timestamp and a format identifier. Store the final
  report beside the generated manifest.
- **The export uses a single timezone.** It is UTC for all dates,
  including dates shown in summaries. Keep it that way.
cases.annotation: The second item contains an explicit dependent pronoun. The source remains available for contextual review.

cases.name: A conditional section and an unresolved imported file
cases.source:
# Before deployment

- Run the full test suite.
- Check the generated manifest.

# General

@.claude/rules/style.md

- Generated documentation must be in English.
cases.annotation: Items under the conditional heading are scored with that heading stated first. A paragraph directly before a list is carried as parent context; an unresolved reference there keeps the item for contextual review. No contextual instruction is silently omitted.

cases.name: An introduced list and an introduction that points back
cases.source:
## Pull requests

When you open a pull request:

- Link the issue.
- Keep the title under 72 characters.

Otherwise:

- Close the branch.
cases.annotation: Each item is scored after its section heading and introduction, and the introduction with its whole list; every range stays on its own lines. An introduction that points back to earlier text is not a complete scope, so it and its item stay for contextual review.

cases.name: A nested item, a numbered procedure, and a nested item that points elsewhere
cases.source:
## Testing

- Keep tests deterministic.
  - Avoid network calls.

## When releasing

1. Update the changelog.
2. Tag the release.

- Run it again:
  - Check the tag.
cases.annotation: A list item is scored together with the items nested under it, and a numbered list as one procedure after the conditional heading it applies under; each range covers the whole block. A nested item whose first line points to other text stays for contextual review.

cases.name: A pronoun resolved in its own excerpt and an instruction to read a linked file
cases.source:
## Setup

If you lack dependencies, install them with `npm ci`.

Read and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

See [the architecture notes](ARCHITECTURE.md) for background.

The build uses one cache. It is cleared nightly.
cases.annotation: A pronoun that follows what it names in the same excerpt, including one that starts a later sentence, and an instruction to read or follow a linked Markdown file, are scored as written; the linked file is not read and the excerpt says so. A link given only for reference stays for contextual review.

cases.name: Command, path and name reference entries
cases.source:
# Commands

Common commands:

- **Run all tests**: `build/sbt test`
- Pregel framework: `build/sbt "testOnly *PregelSuite"`
- `pnpm dev` - start the dev server
- `tests/lisp/` - ERT-style Emacs Lisp tests.

`ASSIGN` - Assignment

`pnpm lint` must pass before committing

Run `pnpm test` before committing.
cases.annotation: A single-line entry that is only a short label and one code span, or one code span and a short description, names a command, path or identifier for reference and is not scored; an introduction whose items are all such entries labels the list. A requirement or condition in the entry or its scope keeps it ready, as do sentences that use a code span.

cases.name: Known arbitrary domain-heading limitation
cases.source:
# Backend

- Use snake_case for field names.

# Frontend

- Use camelCase for field names.
cases.annotation: Backend and Frontend can restrict applicability but are not among the explicit conditional/platform cues. Headings remain separate context; callers must not claim those isolated results establish file-wide consistency or scope. A receiving agent must reassess applicability in the original section.

cases.name: Paragraphs introducing code blocks
cases.source:
## Upgrade

In `build.gradle`, replace:

```gradle
sourceCompatibility = 1.8
```

With:

```gradle
java { toolchain { languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(17) } }
```
cases.annotation: A paragraph ending in a colon is scored with the one code block after it; the block itself stays skipped. "With:" continues the previous step, so it keeps its blocks for contextual review.
